learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and understanding of the engineering disciplines specific to their specialty, at the necessary level to acquire the rest of the competencies of the degree, including notions of the latest advances.
Awareness of the multidisciplinary context of engineering.

Analysis in engineering: The ability to analyze complex products, processes and systems in their field of study; choose and apply relevant established analytical, calculation and experimental methods and correctly interpret the results of said analyses.

Analysis in engineering: The ability to identify, formulate and solve engineering problems in their specialty; appropriately choose and apply established analytical, calculation and experimental methods; recognize the importance of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial constraints.

Engineering projects: Ability to project, design and develop complex products (parts, components, finished products, etc.), processes and systems of their specialty, that meet the established requirements, including awareness of social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial aspects; as well as select and apply appropriate project methods.
Engineering projects: Ability to design using some cutting-edge knowledge of their engineering specialty.

Research and innovation: Ability to conduct bibliographic searches, consult and critically use databases and other information sources, to carry out simulation and analysis with the aim of conducting research on technical topics in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Understanding of applicable techniques and methods of analysis, project and research and their limitations in their specialty.
Practical application of engineering: Knowledge of the social, health and safety, environmental, economic and industrial implications of engineering practice.

Practical application of engineering: General ideas about economic, organizational and management issues (such as project management, risk and change management) in the industrial and business context.
Judgment: Ability to manage complex technical or professional activities or projects in their specialty, taking responsibility for decision-making.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to effectively communicate information, ideas, problems and solutions in the field of engineering and with society in general.
Communication and Teamwork: Ability to function effectively in national and international contexts, individually and in teams, and to cooperate with both engineers and people from other disciplines.
Lifelong learning: Ability to recognize the need for continuous self-training and to undertake this activity throughout their professional life independently.
Lifelong learning: Ability to stay up-to-date with developments in science and technology.
Defines the problem, the development of the solution, as well as the conclusions effectively, arguing and justifying each of them, and making correct use of language, in writing.

teaching_methods: Development, writing, and presentation of reports, memos, audiovisual material, etc. related to projects/POPBLs, carried out individually or in teams
Individual study and work, tests, exams and/or control points
Classroom presentation in participatory classes, of concepts and procedures associated with the subjects

assessment_methods.method: Technical ability, involvement in the project/PBL, work performed, results obtained, documentation submitted, presentation and technical defense
Individual written and oral tests for the evaluation of technical competencies of the subject

assessment_rules: The course uses continuous assessment with project feedback. Resit arrangements use the same assessment methods as the original evaluation.
